headline: New law requires VA budget briefings to Congress, limits bonuses for top VA officials, and creates a Veterans Experience Office through 2028.
what_it_does: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) must brief Congress every three months on its budget, including any shortfalls and its plans to fix them. The VA can no longer give 'critical skill' bonuses to senior executives working in its central headquarters office, and any such bonuses for other senior staff must be approved one person at a time by specific top officials and reported to Congress each year. The law also sets up a Veterans Experience Office through fiscal year 2028 to work on how satisfied veterans are with VA benefits and services. The Government Accountability Office must study how well the VA uses veteran feedback to improve service.

who_it_affects.group: Senior VA executives in the central office
who_it_affects.how: They can no longer receive critical skill bonuses for central office work, though some may still get them for work done at other VA facilities.
Any critical skill bonus must be approved individually by designated top officials, such as the Under Secretary for Health, and is reported to Congress.
A Veterans Experience Office will work through fiscal year 2028 on improving their satisfaction with and use of VA benefits and services.
They will receive quarterly VA budget briefings, including information on shortfalls, plus yearly reports on senior staff bonuses and a GAO report on VA customer service.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted August 14, 2025; the Veterans Experience Office runs through fiscal year 2028.
